RELOCATION PROGRAM PLAN
NORTH-SOUTH FREEWAY (Airport Spur Interchange)
There are a total of twenty-one parcels on the interstate portion of the proposed Airport Spur project. Only one (1) parcel will cause a displacement of a family. There will not be any commercial displacements caused by this proposed project.
The one residential displacement on this proposed project is a single-family ranch home. This home is about six (6) years old. It is a three (3) bedroom brick structure. The occupants of this house are two elderly women, a mother and daughter with an annual income of about $4,500.00. This income is derived from Social Security for the mother of $864.00, self-employment of the daughter of about $1,000.00 and an annual interest income of $2,000.00 to $3,000.00. They have indicated that they wish to purchase another home and not go into a rental situation. They do not have a mortgage on their property.
A survey of an area bounded by Oklahoma Avenue on the north, Ryan Road on the south, South 35th Street on the west and the lake on the east for three bedroom single-family units indicates the following availability: three units in the price range under $20,000.00, seventeen units under $25,000.00, five units under $30,000.00 and eight under $35,000.00. This would indicate that there is available at this time a total of over 33 units. These units are what is available through the Multiple Listing Service. This represents only about fifty percent of the overall market as there are many nonmember brokers active in this area.
A survey in this same area indicated that there were about 95 units sold since the first of the year. A breakdown of this would indicate 21 units under $20,000.00, 41 units under $25,000.00, 24 units under $30,000.00 and 9 units under $35,000.00. This would indicate that there should be good turnover of this type of property during the next year.
